title: Two-Tower Recommender
description: Deep learning recommendation architecture learning separate user and item embeddings in parallel.
name: Two-Tower Recommender
summary: Two-Tower architectures process User features (demographics, history) and Item features (title, category) in separate deep neural networks, projecting both into a shared latent space to compute recommendation candidates via dot-product similarity.
use_when: Building scalable candidate retrieval systems in recommendation pipelines containing millions of items.
avoid_when: Performing final ranking of candidates where fine-grained interaction features are needed.
pros: Enables sub-millisecond retrieval of candidate matches using Approximate Nearest Neighbors.
Can incorporate arbitrary side features (demographics, tags, search terms) easily.
Decoupled towers allow pre-computing and caching item embeddings offline.
cons: Cannot capture complex crossed features (e.g. user-item interactions) in the retrieval layer.
Requires substantial infrastructure to index and search embeddings in real-time.
Highly sensitive to negative sampling strategies during training.

key_hyperparams.name: embedding_dim
key_hyperparams.note: Dimensionality of the shared latent space where user and item embeddings are compared.
